title: CMR 25 105 112 cassava (Rayong 5): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: CMR 25 105 112 cassava: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: CMR 25 105 112 cassava is a cassava variety. 10 to 12 months to harvest, 32.6 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: CMR 25 105 112 is a registered cassava variety, also sold or known as Rayong 5 or Rayong 5 (LSU Cv 15). It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2005 as NSIC 2005 Cv 30. It comes from introduced clone, registered by PhilRootcrops, LSU. It takes 10 to 12 months from planting to harvest, with 32.6 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Rayong 5 or Rayong 5 (LSU Cv 15), this is the same cassava. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [cassava variety finder](/crop-varieties/cassava), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

CMR 25 105 112 cassava takes 10 to 12 months from planting to harvest. That is about the average of the 42 cassava varieties with a day count, 10.5 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 32.6 t/ha matches the average of its group, 32.38. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit cassava fields most often: [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Its roots have white flesh and cream skin. The starch content is 28.1 percent. Its cyanide level, the HCN content, is low. A low level is safer for the table, while a high level calls for peeling, soaking and full cooking. It is recommended for feeds, food, flour and starch processing and ethanol production.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** White flesh, cream skin, dry matter about 40 percent, starch about 28 percent, low HCN.
Most susceptible of tested varieties to cassava phytoplasma disease in PhilRootcrops work.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: introduced clone multiplied for San Miguel's feed and alcohol cassava project in Negros Occidental. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant CMR 25 105 112 cassava

The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country. Pick by buyer first. Starch and feed plants pay for yield and starch content, while the table wants a sweet, low cyanide variety that boils soft. A high starch variety needs a buyer within a day of harvest, because the roots spoil fast.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Rayong 5 the same as CMR 25 105 112?
items.a: Yes. Rayong 5 is another name for CMR 25 105 112, registered as NSIC 2005 Cv 30. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 10 to 12 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 32.6 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of CMR 25 105 112?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
